## Example: Handling personal information ethically (multi-paragraph)

You run a small community forum and receive a user report that someone is sharing another person’s phone number and home address in the comments. Instead of amplifying it, you immediately remove the content, preserve minimal evidence for moderation purposes (e.g., the post ID and timestamp), and warn or suspend the account that posted it.

Next, you review your logs and data access controls to ensure only authorized staff can view user email addresses and IPs. You also update your rules to explicitly prohibit doxxing and harassment, and you provide a “Report abuse” flow that lets victims request removal of personal data quickly.

Finally, you reach out to the affected person with practical steps: document harassment (screenshots/links), tighten privacy settings, and contact the platform or, if there are threats, local authorities. The goal is to reduce harm and protect privacy—not to target anyone.

## Reproducible code example: Redact PII before storing or sharing

```python
import re

PII_PATTERNS = {
    "email": re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b"),
    "phone": re.compile(r"\b(?:\+?\d{1,3}[\s-]?)?(?:\(?\d{2,3}\)?[\s-]?)?\d{3}[\s-]?\d{4}\b"),
}

def redact_pii(text: str) -> str:
    text = PII_PATTERNS["email"].sub("[REDACTED_EMAIL]", text)
    text = PII_PATTERNS["phone"].sub("[REDACTED_PHONE]", text)
    return text

if __name__ == "__main__":
    message = "Contact me at jane.doe@example.com or (555) 123-4567. Don’t post this publicly."
    print("Original:", message)
    print("Redacted:", redact_pii(message))
```
